original_question: For elliptic non-linearizable one-variable germs (Cremer points), are the pair of invariants consisting of (i) the multiplier and (ii) the homeomorphism class of the germ of the stable set at the origin a complete set of topological invariants for topological local conjugacy?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the one-dimensional Cremer-point topological-classification conjecture: whether, for nonlinearizable holomorphic germs with an irrationally indifferent fixed point at 0, the multiplier together with the homeomorphism class of the germ at 0 of the Pérez-Marco stable set (hedgehog) completely determines the local topological conjugacy class.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very closely: it is about one-variable elliptic/nonlinearizable germs (Cremer points), it names exactly the two candidate invariants singled out in the surrounding discussion (the multiplier and the stable-set germ), and it asks the right classification question, namely completeness for topological local conjugacy.
missing_details: Specify the ambient category explicitly: germs of holomorphic local dynamical systems in one complex variable, typically f,g in End(C,0) or Diff(C,0), fixing 0.
State that the fixed point is irrationally indifferent/elliptic and nonlinearizable, i.e. f'(0)=e^{2πiα} with α irrational and f not holomorphically linearizable.
Make explicit that the comparison is between two such germs f and g, and the question is whether equality of the two listed invariants is equivalent to local topological conjugacy.
Clarify that the 'stable set' means the Pérez-Marco stable set, and only its germ at the origin is invariantly defined for the local problem.
Say what 'topologically locally conjugate' means: there exists a homeomorphism between neighborhoods of 0 sending 0 to 0 and conjugating the two germs.
If desired, note that the multiplier may equivalently be phrased as the irrational rotation number α via f'(0)=e^{2πiα}.
Use the paper-faithful scope 'one complex variable' and do not broaden to higher-dimensional indifferent fixed points or to general elliptic germs that may be linearizable.
refined_question: Let f,g be germs of holomorphic local dynamical systems in one complex variable at 0, each having a nonlinearizable irrationally indifferent fixed point at the origin (equivalently, a Cremer point), with multipliers f'(0),g'(0) in S^1\setminus\{roots of unity\}. Let K_f and K_g denote the germs at 0 of their Pérez-Marco stable sets (hedgehogs). Is it true that f and g are topologically locally conjugate if and only if they have the same multiplier and the germs (K_f,0) and (K_g,0) are homeomorphic?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: is the pair consisting of the irrational rotation number α (where f'(0)=e^{2πiα}) and the homeomorphism class of the germ at 0 of the Pérez-Marco stable set a complete set of invariants for local topological conjugacy of one-dimensional nonlinearizable irrationally indifferent holomorphic germs?
justification: The refinement keeps your question at exactly the paper's intended scale: local one-variable holomorphic dynamics at a Cremer point. The nearby context identifies the stable set/hedgehog as the relevant local invariant set, recalls Biswas's holomorphic classification by multiplier plus conformal class of the stable set, recalls Naishul's theorem that the multiplier is a topological invariant, and then isolates the natural remaining open problem asking whether the multiplier together with the homeomorphism class of the stable-set germ is complete for topological classification. The only substantive tightening needed was to make explicit the ambient category, the irrationally indifferent/nonlinearizable hypothesis, the meaning of 'stable set', and the quantifier over pairs of germs.
